subject.title: fix(status): use legacy Codex OAuth profiles for OpenAI usage

question: Should provider-usage runtime auth be allowed to read retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles as a usage-only compatibility bridge, or should affected users be required to run `openclaw doctor --fix` first?
rationale: Repository policy normally keeps legacy provider ids in doctor/migration paths, but the PR has concrete proof that a shipped legacy-only auth store loses status usage without this runtime exception.

options.title: Accept usage-only bridge
options.body: Allow `status --usage` to read legacy `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles while still reporting canonical `openai` usage.

options.title: Keep doctor-only migration
options.body: Pause or close this PR and keep runtime strict, requiring users to run `openclaw doctor --fix` before usage status reads those profiles.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Ask for an additional patch or comment that names the temporary boundary and removal/migration expectation before accepting the fallback.

recommendation.title: Accept usage-only bridge
recommendation.body: Allow `status --usage` to read legacy `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles while still reporting canonical `openai` usage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the OpenAI provider identity migration and runtime-vs-doctor legacy boundary that this owner most directly touched.
